thread.title: Gen Z Protesters Surge in New Delhi Against Modi Government
thread.title_full: Gen Z Protesters Surge in New Delhi Against Modi Government

author: ethan.brook News Editor
title: Gen Z Protesters Surge in New Delhi Against Modi Government
text:
Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s government faces its biggest challenge yet in 12 years in power as tens of thousands of people take to the streets of New Delhi to protest the deletion of 130 million voter roll names.
Street protests across India this year are on track to outpace any period in the past decade, according to data from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project.
Voter Purges and the Conflict Over the Electoral Roll The current unrest exploded over an Election Commission verification exercise that removed 130 million voters from the national rolls . Opposition parties and demonstrators argue that the deletions disproportionately target Muslim voters and other minorities unlikely to support the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party. The controversy centers on Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, whose resignation protesters have demanded alongside a complete halt and rollback of the Special Intensive Revision exercise.
Rise of the Cockroach Janta Party and the July Ouster of Dharmendra Pradhan The resistance draws its energy largely from a parody social media movement founded by political communications strategist Abhijeet Dipke. Dubbed the Cockroach Janta Party, the youth group formed over the summer in response to leaked question papers and widespread irregularities in national examinations. The movement embraced the satirical label cockroaches after Chief Justice Surya Kant used the term during a Supreme Court hearing on May 15.
Photo: Scroll.in If you’re so determined to crush dissent, have the courage to officially declare an Emergency instead of hiding behind these cowardly tactics.
Abhijeet Dipke, CJP founder
The CJP’s initial mobilization forced a stunning concession in July when nationwide student protests successfully ousted Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan following the cancellation of medical school entrance examinations. Ministerial resignations are exceptionally rare in the country, making that capitulation a historic blow to Modi’s strongman image.
Delhi Lockdown and the Confrontation at Jantar Mantar In response to the resurgent demonstrations, the government transformed the national capital into a fortress. Last Saturday, authorities deployed 40,000 security personnel, shut down 57 metro stations, erected barricades across the city center, and severed internet access in protest zones. Economist Jean Drèze, detained by police during the demonstrations, observed that in nearly 50 years in India he had never witnessed such heavy use of force to quell public dissent.
Photo: Al Jazeera Despite tear gas, baton charges, and mass arrests of thousands of protesters, the youth demonstrated extraordinary resilience.
Ananya Raturi, a 21-year-old Delhi University student, stated that the fear in them is gone and they do not fear being detained or beaten up by the police.
Economic Pressures and the Growing Grievance Over Jobs and Inflation Beyond democratic grievances, the protests channel deep-seated economic anxiety. Unemployment among graduates aged 15 to 25 approaches 40 percent according to the Azim Premji University State of Working India report, while about one in five graduates aged 25 to 29 remain jobless.
Instagram Rahul Verma, a fellow at the Centre for Policy Research in New Delhi, notes that while the BJP underperformed in the 2024 general election and faces a tough test in the upcoming Uttar Pradesh state polls, predicting immediate national electoral consequences remains premature. With Modi celebrating his 25th year in public office since taking charge as Gujarat chief minister in October 2001, the durability of this Gen Z uprising presents the most formidable challenge yet to his administration.
